key_numbers.metric: knowledge-enhancement effect on F1 (Solidity, foundation models)
key_numbers.value: F1 nearly doubling on average with knowledge vs. without

key_numbers.metric: context-supplementation effect on TP counts across 36 knowledge x prompt combinations
key_numbers.value: Solidity 22/36 increased, Java 18/36 increased, C/C++ 28/36 increased
14 confirmed vulnerabilities of 29 submitted, $3,576 in bounties across 4 projects

structure_gain: Context supplementation (caller/related-function context) increased TP in 22/36 (Solidity), 18/36 (Java), 28/36 (C/C++) knowledge x prompt combinations vs. the no-context condition, same model/budget (RQ2).
confound_note: Knowledge (Nk/Ok/Sk), context (with/without), and prompt scheme (raw/CoT) are each varied independently while holding the model and the other two dimensions fixed within each comparison cell -- a genuine 3-way representation/context ablation across 6 LLMs and 3 languages.
stop_detail: Caller/related-function context is statically extracted and serialized directly into the prompt; knowledge grounding uses either the LLM's own knowledge, raw retrieved vulnerability reports (FAISS top-3), or GPT-4.1-summarized knowledge, per the knowledge/context prompt templates (Fig. 4, Sec. III-IV).
threats_to_datum: Context is supplied via static analysis 'for benchmarking purposes only' rather than real agentic retrieval; retrieved knowledge itself is imperfectly aligned with ground truth (only 36-68% of sampled retrieved knowledge matched ground truth), which could understate the true achievable benefit of context/knowledge.

structure_gain: No raw-source-text baseline is reported; all three evaluated methods (BERT, DistilBERT, LSTM) use the LLVM-IR representation. Against prior tool VulDeeLocator: 98.25% vs. 82.43% accuracy, but method/representation/training pipeline differ simultaneously.
confound_note: The comparison is against a prior tool (VulDeeLocator) rather than an ablation of the same model with/without the LLVM-IR + interprocedural-slice representation; architecture, training data, and representation all vary together, so no isolated representation effect can be attributed.
stop_detail: Source code is compiled to LLVM IR; for each function call the callee's IR is spliced into the caller at the call site (interprocedural composition) before tokenization and fine-tuning of BERT/DistilBERT/LSTM (preprocessing/iSeVC construction section).
threats_to_datum: No ablation isolates the IR representation itself from the model architecture; gains over VulDeeLocator may stem from the transformer architectures rather than the representation. Programs are truncated to under 265 lines of IR, and no F1/precision/recall are reported alongside accuracy.

datasets: custom benchmark of 15 real-world C/C++ projects
9 additional high-profile OSS projects (real-world validation set)
structure_gain: With structured data-flow abstraction (memory of feasible-path/data-flow-fact tuples) vs. without (RepoAudit-NoAbs): precision 78.43% (40TP/11FP) vs. 40.38% (21TP/31FP); with validator vs. without: 78.43% vs. 33.33%, same LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), same benchmark (Table 6).
confound_note: Table 6 ablations vary only one component at a time (program abstraction on/off; validator on/off) holding the LLM and benchmark fixed -- a clean representation/verification-only ablation.
stop_detail: Demand-driven, call-graph-guided exploration produces LLM-derived data-flow facts (u@s -> v@s notation) along feasible paths, cached in an agent memory keyed by (function, value); a validator cross-checks control-flow ordering and path feasibility before reporting (Explorer/Validator sections, Table 6).
threats_to_datum: Interprocedural analysis is explicitly bounded to a maximum calling-context depth of 4 functions and the authors state RepoAudit 'is not sound' for longer call chains; residual false positives/negatives from LLM hallucination persist despite the validator.

key_numbers.metric: F1-score improvement, context selection vs. full-function ablation (w/o CS)

structure_gain: FocusVul with CPG-derived dependency/execution-flow context selection vs. w/o CS (full-function baseline), same LM: +164.03% avg F1 improvement and -25.03% avg VDS@0.5 on PrimeVul (ablation table).
confound_note: The w/o VC (no commit-supervision), w/o VCI (no VRR prediction at inference), and w/o CS (full function, no context selection) ablations hold the base LM fixed and vary only the context-construction pipeline, isolating the representation/context-selection effect from model capacity.
stop_detail: Vulnerability-Relevant Regions are identified from commit-fix diffs via hierarchical semantic modeling, then a slice around these regions is extracted from the Code Property Graph using control/data-dependence and execution-order edges before fine-tuning a standard LM on the sliced segments (context extraction / methodology section).
threats_to_datum: IMPORTANT: this paper was withdrawn by the author on arXiv citing 'fundamental errors in the methodology' (per the arXiv abstract-page withdrawal notice). The extraction above is drawn from the (withdrawn) v1 full text; reported numbers should be treated as unreliable pending author correction, not as a validated representation-only-ablation datum. Joern also fails to parse ~9.84% of functions.

datasets: custom benchmark (14 real-world projects, 49 memory errors)

key_numbers.metric: correct patches, full LTFix vs. LTFix-NT (no context trace) ablation
total errors fixed, full LTFix vs. LTFix-F (file-level context) ablation
repair success rate (custom benchmark / SAVER dataset)

structure_gain: Full LTFix (typestate-guided context trace) vs. LTFix-NT (error-propagation path only, no context trace), same LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet): 22 vs. 15 correct patches (+47%), 37 vs. 22 total errors fixed (+68%), 1 vs. 4 new errors introduced (Section 5.7 ablation, RQ3).
confound_note: The LTFix-F / LTFix-M / LTFix-NT / full ablation fixes the LLM and prompting strategy, varying only the amount/structure of retrieved context (implicated files -> backtrace functions -> propagation path without trace -> full typestate-guided context trace), isolating the context-representation effect.
stop_detail: A finite typestate automaton instruments dynamic execution (via GDB) to record memory-object state transitions only at typestate-changing statements, producing an error-propagation path (nearest allocation to error point) and a context trace that are serialized into the LLM prompt (Algorithm 1, methodology section).
threats_to_datum: Evaluation relies on dynamic analysis requiring proof-of-concept inputs, so errors not exercised by available PoCs are missed; multi-threaded programs are explicitly excluded; LLM output validity is determined by a majority-of-5-runs threshold (4/5), introducing residual non-determinism.

structure_gain: Verification/fusion module reported to outperform LLM-only and RAG-only baselines by 'at least 4% (vs. LLM) and 12% (vs. RAG)' in F1 for single-label detection (Figure 4); exact per-configuration numbers not stated in the accessible text.
confound_note: The fusion condition changes retrieval strategy (dense/BM25/none) AND adds a meta-learning verification layer simultaneously relative to the SLoRA-only LLM baseline, so the retrieval/context effect is not cleanly isolated from the added fusion mechanism.
stop_detail: Hybrid retrieval (dense embeddings over sliding-window segments + BM25) over a corpus of labeled vulnerable code fragments supplies inherited vulnerability labels that are fused with the SLoRA-fine-tuned LLM's prediction via a meta-learning MLP, rather than being concatenated into the LLM's prompt (retrieval/fusion methodology section).
threats_to_datum: Figure 4's LLM-only/RAG-only/fusion comparison does not hold the base LLM or the presence of the fusion/verification layer constant across arms, so gains cannot be attributed specifically to retrieval-augmented context vs. the meta-learning fusion component; exact numeric values for Figure 4 were not visible in the fetched text.

key_numbers.metric: virtualization-obfuscation attack success rate (downgrade), C/C++ datasets
detection success-rate gap, existence-only vs. type+location scoring criterion
key_numbers.value: ~40% average increase under existence-only vs. type/location criterion

structure_gain: Central ablation compares raw code text vs. its obfuscated (layout/data-flow/control-flow-transformed) counterpart, same LLM/prompt: virtualization obfuscation degrades detection with up to ~80% attack success rate on C/C++ (Finding #2); conversely some layout obfuscations (e.g., L1) 'upgrade' detection by removing misleading surface cues, e.g. QWEN-14B on PrimeVul jumps from 0.39 to 0.80 success after L1 (Section 4.2.3).
confound_note: Table 6's original-vs-obfuscated comparison holds the LLM, prompt template, and underlying ground-truth vulnerability fixed and varies only the raw-text obfuscation transformation -- a clean representation-only ablation, though 'representation' here means raw-text surface form (layout/data-flow/control-flow perturbation) rather than a structured alternative such as AST or CFG.
stop_detail: No external grounding/retrieval mechanism is used; detection is single-turn prompting of raw (possibly obfuscated) source code, scored on a 1-4 rubric checking existence, type, and location match against ground truth (Section 4.1 Evaluation Metrics).
threats_to_datum: Obfuscation transformations are generated by GPT-4o itself rather than a verified-correctness obfuscation tool, so semantic preservation of the obfuscated code is not independently confirmed; temperature fixed near zero for reproducibility, but reasoning-model output variance is not otherwise addressed.

key_numbers.metric: F1 ablation on PrimeVul, full vs. w/o graph optimizer

structure_gain: Full VulnAgent-R2 (bounded graph-context optimizer) vs. w/o graph optimizer, same base LLM (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B), on PrimeVul: F1 0.385 vs. 0.337 (Table 10); w/o CER 0.359, w/o Sceptic 0.352, w/o VPS 0.346 -- each context/verification component contributes measurably.
confound_note: Table 10 removes one architectural component (graph optimizer / counterfactual evidence reweighting / Sceptic / verification-plan synthesis) at a time while holding the base LLM and remaining pipeline fixed, isolating each context/verification mechanism's marginal contribution to F1.
stop_detail: Grounded via a Joern-style code property graph (AST+CFG+DFG+CALL edges) traversed under a token-budgeted, greedy utility-maximizing selection (Eq. 6) that pulls in callers, callees, data-flow neighbors, tests, configs, and historical patches; claims are further calibrated via counterfactual evidence reweighting and executable verification harnesses (graph triage / CER / VPS sections).
threats_to_datum: Authors caution PrimeVul F1 remains modest (0.385) and describe the system as 'a prioritization aid rather than a replacement for manual review'; some ablation deltas are small relative to likely LLM sampling variance, and build-environment/runtime-assumption failures account for 23.8% of errors.

key_numbers.metric: false positives, QASecClaw vs. standalone Semgrep

structure_gain: QASecClaw (SAST + LLM file-context filter agent) vs. standalone Semgrep on the same OWASP Benchmark v1.2 test set: F1 90.93% vs. 78.39%, precision 95.1% vs. 69.5%, false positives 64 vs. 560 (-88.6%), recall 87.1% vs. 90.0% (-3.2 pp).
confound_note: The comparison is standalone-SAST vs. the full LLM-agent pipeline added at once; no ablation isolates the raw-file-context contribution itself (e.g., LLM-with-context vs. LLM-without-context) from the broader multi-agent orchestration (Mission Orchestrator, validators) introduced simultaneously.
stop_detail: The SAST Filter Agent builds a per-finding prompt containing the CWE category, file location, and the complete relevant source-file text (batched 15 files at a time), queries Qwen 3.5 Plus, and parses a structured JSON true/false-positive verdict (Methodology section).
threats_to_datum: Evaluated only on a synthetic benchmark (OWASP Benchmark v1.2), a single language (Java), and a single SAST baseline (Semgrep), with no repeated-run or multi-model robustness check; the Trust Boundary Violation (CWE-501) category regressed relative to Semgrep alone.

key_numbers.metric: out-of-distribution repair success rate (Vul4J, 23 unseen CWEs)

structure_gain: No ablation isolates the retrieval/Curator-Agent context contribution; authors report only end-to-end repair success rate vs. other repair tools (Table III: RAVEN 7/9 correct vs. fewer for SAN2PATCH/PatchAgent on unseen C vulnerabilities), so no representation-only delta is available.
confound_note: Comparison against baseline repair tools (SAN2PATCH, PatchAgent, ExtractFix, VulnFix, VulMaster) varies the entire pipeline (LLM, retrieval, agent architecture) simultaneously; the retrieval/context contribution is not isolated from model and pipeline differences.
stop_detail: A Curator Agent iteratively calls repository-exploration tools (read_bundle, search_repo, find_symbol, read_file) to gather cross-file caller/callee and dependency information, combined with a multi-faceted BM25 retriever (keyword, code-snippet, and Joern-CPG based) whose top patch is chosen by a Selector Agent and injected into the Patch Generator's prompt (Algorithm 1 / Curator Agent section).
threats_to_datum: Authors explicitly note no per-component ablation isolates the retrieval/Curator-Agent contribution; 'partial fixes' count toward the reported success rate, and CodeBLEU similarity does not guarantee functional/security correctness; performance drops substantially out-of-distribution (65.22% vs. 86.75%).

structure_gain: Full CLEAR (with Vulnerability Causal Knowledge Graph context) vs. No-VCKG ablation, same multi-agent LLM pipeline, on PrimeVul: Pairwise-Correct 19.17 vs. 8.08 (Table 3); removing only Fix-Intent nodes drops it to 14.32 vs. 19.17 full.
confound_note: Table 3's node-ablation removes individual VCKG node types (or the whole VCKG) while holding the multi-agent (Collector/Claim/Critic/Judge) architecture and base LLM fixed, isolating the causal-context representation's contribution; the headline 130.7%/71.56% figures instead compare CLEAR's full pipeline against a different prior system (VulTrial), which is not representation-isolated.
stop_detail: Grounded via a Vulnerability Causal Knowledge Graph built offline from CVE descriptions, patches, and source code (LLM-extracted causal chains linked by semantic-similarity neighborhood edges and cross-instance global edges); a Collector Agent retrieves the Top-5 similar historical Entrypoints and traverses Local/Neighbor/Global edges, serializing the result into the Claim/Critic/Judge agents' prompts (VCKG construction / Collector Agent section).
threats_to_datum: Authors note semantic similarity used to build VCKG edges does not guarantee causal consistency (nodes can be linked despite being causally unrelated, or left disconnected despite sharing a mechanism); human inter-rater agreement on Global Edge validity is only moderate (kappa=0.51); causal claims are LLM-derived, not symbolically verified.
